##API Demo: USA Jobs

```{r}
# var request = require('request');

#usethis::edit_r_environ("project") type this into terminal to connect API environment key; creates .renviron file to save keys

host = 'data.usajobs.gov'
user_Agent = 'ellingrj@miamioh.edu'
auth_key = Sys.getenv('USJOBS_API_KEY') #built in function to pull the API key from the R environment

req = httr2::request('https://data.usajobs.gov/api/search') |>
  httr2::req_method("GET") |>
  httr2::req_url_query(
    JobCategoryCode=2210, # showing an ex similar to the doc
    Keyword = "Data Analyst", # we are asked to find data analyst jobs
    #could have also added location name, but we were not asked to 
    ResultsPerPage = 500
    ) |>
  httr2::req_headers(
    #left hand side is the name from the argument for the request headers per the API
    #RHS is the name of the object as we created it in R
    Host = host, 
    `User-Agent` = user_Agent, #R does not like spaces of dashes, so we use the back tick to tell it that that is a name
    `Authorization-Key` = auth_key
    
  )

response = httr2::req_perform(req) #executes the request and gets a response back

#getting the data out of the response

#response$body 
#quick view of what our data is

usajobs_data = response |>
  httr2::resp_body_json()
 

usajobs_data

#also acceptable
usajobs_data = response |>
  httr2::resp_body_string() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(flatten = T)

#usajobs_data # returned a nested list, which we examined in the environment viewer (clicked the var in the global envir)
dplyr::glimpse(usajobs_data) # not nice, but another way to see it

#from the glimpse, we saw Search Result Items was a df

usajobs_df <- usajobs_data$SearchResult$SearchResultItems |>
# by looking at the data in the global environment, we can see many cols in this df have more dfs
# to pull list cols from the data (i.e. a col that has a df)
  #just an ex, didn't remove all the problem children 
tidyr::unnest(
  cols = c("MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionLocation", "MatchedObjectDescriptor.JobCategory", "MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionOfferingType" ), 
  names_sep = '.' # this chooses what will be added to create unique names (basically from my undertsanding it takes the outer name and inner name and creates a new name that is both separated by a . )
              )
#names(usajobs_df)


# to answer the question in the slides, there are 31 available data analyst jobs
# be careful, it says 32 obs but only 31 unique job ids (our nest split one job with several locations into 2 rows)


#this is my attempt to remove the duplicate, its not ideal but it works
unique_jobs <- usajobs_data$SearchResult$SearchResultItems

table(unique_jobs$MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName)


#to do it with a package
#no real solution for duplicates yet
usajobs_df |>
  dplyr:: count(MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName)
# solution for duplicates is added to the lesson

```

1. To answer the question on the slides, there are 31 federally available data analyst related jobs. 
Found using `unique(usajobs_df$MatchedObjectId) |> length()`
